title: Word RAM execution
statement: For a word width $W$, a program $P$ consisting of word RAM instructions, a fuel amount $t$, a program counter $pc$, and a memory assigning a $W$-bit word to each integer address, execution returns either no result or a Boolean outcome together with the resulting memory. With zero fuel it returns no result. With positive fuel it executes the instruction at $pc$, treating a position beyond the program as a rejection: arithmetic and memory operations update the designated cell and continue at the next position, a conditional jump changes the next position according to whether the tested word represents a negative integer, and acceptance or rejection returns the corresponding outcome with memory unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: memory maps integer addresses to $W$-bit words
